newsitem.title: USA: Minn Gov asks special session for Twins stadium.
newsitem.headline: Minn Gov asks special session for Twins stadium.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson said Monday he intends to call lawmakers to a special session in September to consider financing for a new ballpark for the Minnesota Twins American League baseball club.

"The Twins ownership has made it abundantly clear that they cannot wait for the 1998 legislative session and that they very likely will give notice on Oct 1 of their plan to move the club to another city," Carlson said in a letter to lawmakers.

Carlson, a strong supporter of a new stadium for the team, said legislators will have ample time to discuss funding proposals for a new ballpark over the summer and prepare themselves for a short session.

The Republican governor had proposed a 10-cent-per-pack cigarette tax hike over five years to finance a new ballpark. Carlson's plan included the state receiving a 49 percent ownership stake in the team and retaining ownership of a new retractable roof stadium worth an estimated $350 million to $400 million.
Legislators rejected numerous ballpark financing plans during their session concluded in mid-May without a full vote of either the Senate or House of Representatives.
Twins owner Carl Pohlad announced May 27 the team would explore other options, including a possible sale and relocation.
Pohlad stated that he would consider legislative solutions before the end of the 1997 baseball season, but would not wait for a decision in the 1998 legislative session.

"This week, Mr. Pohlad will meet with major league baseball's executive council to receive permission to begin pursuing his relocation options," Carlson wrote. "If we as a state have any intentions of keeping this team, it is imperative that we deal with this issue in the next several months."
